rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report depicts believers returning home after sitting with the Lord, where their wives welcome them and find them more beautiful and fragrant.
rows.anchor: مرحبا وأهلا بحبنا، لقد جئت وإن بك من الجمال والطيب

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the report uncommon and says it is known only through this route; Ibn Majah also transmits a similar version.
rows.anchor: هذا حديث غريب، لا نعرفه إلا من هذا الوجه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said God welcomes those who welcome meeting Him; this means a believer receives glad tidings and longs to meet God, while a wicked person hears of evil and recoils.
rows.anchor: من أحب لقاء الله أحب الله لقاءه، ومن كره لقاء الله كره الله لقاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir grades the report authentic and notes that it appears in the Sahih by another route.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في الصحيح من غير هذا الوجه

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن والسدي والضحاك
rows.claim: They explain ships sailing in the sea like al-aʿlām as looking like mountains on land.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد، والحسن، والسدي، والضحاك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can stop the wind that drives ships, leaving them motionless on the water, unable to come or go.
rows.anchor: يسكن الريح} أي: التي تسير بالسفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The controlled sea and wind display divine blessings: the steadfast endure hardship and the grateful give thanks in ease.
rows.anchor: أي: في الشدائد، {شكور} في الرخاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could destroy ships because of their passengers’ sins, but forgives many; if He took them for every sin, all who sailed would perish.
rows.anchor: ولو أخذهم بجميع ذنوبهم لأهلك كل من ركب البحر

rows.speaker: بعض علماء التفسير
rows.claim: Some exegetes say God could send a fierce wind that diverts ships from their straight course and destination.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض علماء التفسير: معنى قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This alternative also entails destruction and fits the first interpretation: God may stop the wind or strengthen it until ships stray and perish.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو يتضمن هلاكها، وهو مناسب للأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In mercy, God sends wind and rain according to need; excess rain would ruin buildings, while Egypt receives flowing water from elsewhere because rain would damage its walls.
rows.anchor: ورحمته أنه يرسله بحسب الحاجة، كما يرسل المطر بقدر الكفاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet can only convey the message, not guide the deaf or blind; God guides or misguides whom He wills with just judgment.
rows.anchor: ليس ذلك إليك، إنما عليك البلاغ، وليس عليك هداهم، ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi understands the threat to mean God will punish the opponents whether the Prophet dies first or lives to witness it; Ibn Jarir chooses this view.
rows.anchor: هذا معنى قول السدي، واختاره ابن جرير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says the Prophet died while vengeance remained; unlike other prophets, he did not see anything hateful from his community, though he was shown what would befall it afterward.
rows.anchor: ذهب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبقيت النقمة،

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith compares the stars as security for heaven and the Prophet as security for his Companions: after each is gone, the promised trial comes.
rows.anchor: النجوم أمنة للسماء، فإذا ذهبت النجوم أتى السماء ما توعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must hold fast to the Qur’an revealed to his heart: it is truth and guides to God’s straight path, Paradise, and lasting good.
rows.anchor: خذ بالقرآن المنزل على قلبك، فإنه هو الحق، وما يهدي إليه هو الحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: They explain the Qur’an as an honor for the Prophet and his people; Ibn Jarir prefers this meaning and cites no other.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والسدي، وابن زيد.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Muawiya says leadership remains among Quraysh, and anyone who contests it while they uphold religion will be cast down; al-Bukhari records it.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الأمر في قريش لا ينازعهم فيه أحد إلا أكبه الله على وجهه ما أقاموا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns and governs the heavens and earth in this world and the next; when the Hour comes, falsehood’s adherents lose, meaning disbelievers who deny God and His clear proofs.
rows.anchor: أنه مالك السموات والأرض، الحاكم فيهما

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan rebuked al-Maʿafiri for amusing people by reminding him of the Day when falsehood’s adherents lose; the saying remained associated with him until his death.
rows.anchor: يا شيخ، أما علمت أن لله يوما يخسر فيه المبطلون؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation will kneel from the terror and gravity of the scene.
rows.anchor: أي: على ركبها من الشدة والعظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that when Hell roars, all people kneel, including Abraham and Jesus, each pleading only for himself; Jesus says he will not ask for Mary.
rows.anchor: لا يبقى أحد إلا جثا لركبتيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وكعب الأحبار والحسن البصري
rows.claim: They take every nation being gathered on its knees literally.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وكعب الأحبار، والحسن البصري:

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrimah says the nations are separated on their respective sides, not kneeling; Ibn Kathir says the first interpretation is preferable.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: {جاثية} متميزة على ناحيتها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Babah says the Prophet could see the people kneeling in heaps before Hell.
rows.anchor: كأني أراكم جاثين بالكوم دون جهنم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a marfuʿ report about the divine image, Abu Hurayra says people are sorted and nations kneel, identifying this as the verse’s scene; Ibn Kathir says this joins both interpretations without conflict.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، مرفوعا في حديث الصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nation is summoned to its record of deeds, as in the scene where the Book is set down and prophets and witnesses are brought.
rows.anchor: يعني: كتاب أعمالها، كقوله: {ووضع الكتاب وجيء بالنبيين والشهداء}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are repaid for both the good and bad they did, as the Qur’an says a person is informed of what was sent ahead and left behind and is witness against himself.
rows.anchor: أي: تجازون بأعمالكم خيرها وشرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record presents all deeds truthfully, adding and omitting nothing, as another verse says the Book misses no small or great deed.
rows.anchor: جميع أعمالكم من غير زيادة ولا نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God means that He commanded the guardian angels to write people’s deeds.
rows.anchor: إنا كنا نأمر الحفظة أن تكتب أعمالكم عليكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Angels write deeds, take them to heaven, and compare them with the record based on what God wrote in the Preserved Tablet before creation, with no letter added or removed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: تكتب الملائكة أعمال العباد، ثم تصعد بها إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning His judgment of believers and disbelievers, God is praised as owner of the heavens, earth, and all worlds.
rows.anchor: أي: المالك لهما وما فيهما؛ ولهذا قال:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains God’s الكبرياء as sovereignty; all things submit to Him and need Him.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني السلطان. أي: هو العظيم الممجد، الذي كل شيء خاضع لديه فقير إليه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound hadith says God’s greatness and pride are His cloak and mantle, and whoever contests either will be placed in Hell; Muslim transmits it from Abu Hurayra and Abu Saʿid.
rows.anchor: العظمة إزاري والكبرياء ردائي، فمن نازعني واحدا منهما أسكنته ناري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAziz is unconquerable, and al-Hakim is wise in His words, deeds, law, and decree.
rows.anchor: أي: الذي لا يغالب ولا يمانع، {الحكيم} في أقواله وأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding command to worship God alone and remain upright, the Qur’an pairs that with kindness to parents, tenderness, and care, as it does elsewhere.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى في الآية الأولى التوحيد له وإخلاص العبادة والاستقامة إليه، عطف بالوصية بالوالدين

rows.speaker: سعد
rows.claim: Saʿd’s mother refused food and drink until he disbelieved, saying God commanded obedience to parents; after she was forced to eat, the verse about kindness to parents was revealed.
rows.anchor: قالت أم سعد لسعد: أليس قد أمر الله بطاعة الوالدين، فلا آكل طعاما، ولا أشرب شرابا حتى تكفر بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim and the Sunan collections except Ibn Majah transmit this account through Shuʿba with the same chain, in a longer form.
rows.anchor: ورواه مسلم وأهل السنن إلا ابن ماجه، من حديث شعبة بإسناده، نحوه وأطول منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pregnancy brings nausea, illness, heaviness, distress, and other hardship, while childbirth also involves the difficulty and pain of labor.
rows.anchor: من وحام وغشيان وثقل وكرب، إلى غير ذلك مما تنال الحوامل من التعب والمشقة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali combines the thirty months of pregnancy and weaning with the two-year weaning period to infer a six-month minimum pregnancy; Ibn Kathir calls the deduction strong and correct.
rows.anchor: على أن أقل مدة الحمل ستة أشهر، وهو استنباط قوي صحيح

rows.speaker: عثمان وجماعة من الصحابة
rows.claim: Uthman and a group of Companions agreed with Ali’s deduction that pregnancy can last as little as six months.
rows.anchor: ووافقه عليه عثمان وجماعة من الصحابة

rows.speaker: بعجة بن عبد الله الجهني
rows.claim: A woman from his tribe delivered after six months; Uthman ordered her stoned until Ali showed from the Qur’an that six months was possible, but she had already been delivered. Her husband recognized the child, and the report says he later died from a consuming ulcer.
rows.anchor: فولدت له لتمام ستة أشهر، فانطلق زوجها إلى عثمان فذكر ذلك له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calculates that a nine-month birth needs twenty-one months of nursing, a seven-month birth twenty-three, and a six-month birth two full years, totaling thirty months.
rows.anchor: إذا وضعت المرأة لتسعة أشهر كفاه من الرضاع أحد وعشرون شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The child’s full strength comes with adulthood; by forty, reason, understanding, and judgment are complete, and people generally do not change much afterward.
rows.anchor: أي: قوي وشب وارتجل {وبلغ أربعين سنة}

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq says a man is called to account for his sins upon reaching forty and should be on guard.
rows.anchor: قلت لمسروق: متى يؤخذ الرجل بذنوبه؟ قال: إذا بلغت الأربعين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Uthman says a Muslim’s reckoning is eased at forty, repentance is granted at sixty, heaven’s inhabitants love him at seventy, good deeds are fixed and sins erased at eighty, and forgiveness and intercession come at ninety.
rows.anchor: العبد المسلم إذا بلغ أربعين سنة خفف الله حسابه

rows.speaker: الحجاج بن عبد الله الحكمي
rows.claim: The Umayyad official says he left sins for forty years out of shame before people, then continued leaving them out of shame before God.
rows.anchor: تركت المعاصي والذنوب أربعين سنة حياء من الناس، ثم تركتها حياء من الله

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The quoted poet describes a man who turned away from falsehood once gray hair covered his head.
rows.anchor: صبا ما صبا حتى علا الشيب رأسه … فلما علاه قال للباطل: ابطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awziʿni means inspire me; the prayer asks for gratitude for God’s favors to the speaker and parents, pleasing righteous work, and the reform of descendants.
rows.anchor: أي: ألهمني {أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse guides anyone reaching forty to renew repentance and return firmly to God.
rows.anchor: وهذا فيه إرشاد لمن بلغ الأربعين أن يجدد التوبة والإنابة إلى الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports a supplication the Prophet taught in tashahhud, asking for united hearts, peace, protection from wrong, blessings on family and senses, repentance, and gratefulness.
rows.anchor: كان يعلمهم أن يقولوا في التشهد:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as repentant and returning to God have their best deeds accepted and sins overlooked; God forgives many faults and accepts even modest work.
rows.anchor: هم الذين يتقبل عنهم أحسن ما عملوا، ويتجاوز عن سيئاتهم، فيغفر لهم الكثير من الزلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be among the people of Paradise, fulfilling God’s true promise to those who repent and turn back to Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا حكمهم عند الله كما وعد الله من تاب إليه وأناب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports through the Prophet and Gabriel that a servant’s good and bad deeds are balanced; if one good deed remains, God expands his place in Paradise.
rows.anchor: بعضها ببعض، فإن بقيت حسنة وسع الله له في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim repeats the report attributed to Ibn Abbas through another transmission and adds that God Himself says the deeds will be brought; Ibn Kathir calls it uncommon but gives its chain a good, acceptable grade.
rows.anchor: وهو حديث غريب، وإسناد جيد لا بأس به

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Hatib says Ali, with Ammar, Saʿsaʿa, al-Ashtar, and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr present, declared Uthman among those whose best deeds God accepts and whose sins He overlooks, repeating the judgment three times.
rows.anchor: فقال علي: كان عثمان من الذين قال الله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away means retreating from jihad; corruption and severing kinship mean reverting to pre-Islamic bloodshed and broken family ties.
rows.anchor: أي: عن الجهاد ونكلتم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse forbids corruption generally and severing family ties specifically, while commanding reform and kindness to relatives through words, deeds, and money.
rows.anchor: وهذا نهي عن الإفساد في الأرض عموما، وعن قطع الأرحام خصوصا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that kinship sought refuge from severance, and God promised to join those who maintain it and cut off those who sever it; the Prophet linked this to the verse, and Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
rows.anchor: ألا ترضين أن أصل من وصلك وأقطع من قطعك؟ قالت: بلى. قال: فذاك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Bakra reports that oppression and severing kinship are especially likely to bring punishment quickly in this life as well as the next; al-Tirmidhi grades the report authentic.
rows.anchor: ما من ذنب أحرى أن يعجل الله عقوبته في الدنيا، مع ما يدخر لصاحبه في الآخرة، من البغي وقطيعة الرحم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Thawban reports that whoever wants a longer life and increased provision should maintain family ties; Ahmad transmits it alone here, with a supporting report in the Sahih.
rows.anchor: من سره النساء في الأجل، والزيادة في الرزق، فليصل رحمه
